newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mitsui says Singapore sales set to double.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui says Singapore sales set to double.

text.p: Integrated circuit frame maker Mitsui High-tec Inc said on Wednesday sales from Singapore would more than double to Singapore $175.0 million over the next five years.
It said sales would be boosted by building a new S$80.0 million plant and making Singapore Mitsui's regional for Asia outside Japan headquarters, it said.
"Total investment for this expansion is estimated at S$80.0 million, which is expected to generate more than S$100.0 million of new sales and 300 new jobs," the company said in a statement.
Sales from Mitsui's Singapore operations were about S$75.0 million in 1996 and its current plant employs about 200 people.
The projections were made at the official groundbreaking of the site for the first phase of Mitsui's new regional headquarters and manufacturing plant in Tuas, Singapore.
Phase one is expected to be complete by 1998, with a second phase estimated to be finished by 2003 when the lease on the company's existing Singapore plant runs out, the statement said.
Once phase one is built, Singapore would become responsible for Mitsui operations in Malaysia, Hong Kong and the Philippines.
China operations could also fall under the Singapore umbrella at a later stage, a company spokesman said.
Mitsui's sales turnover was about US$500.0 million in 1996. About 30 percent of this figure was generated outside Japan.
